```{r}
library(fpp3)

beer <- aus_production |>
  filter(year(Quarter) >= 2000) |>
  select(Quarter, Beer)

fit <- beer |>
  model(
    Mean   = MEAN(Beer),
    Naive  = NAIVE(Beer),
    SNaive = SNAIVE(Beer),
    Drift  = RW(Beer ~ drift())
  )

fit |>
  forecast(h = 16) |>
  autoplot(beer, level = NULL) +
  labs(
    title = "Four benchmark forecasts for Australian beer production",
    y = "Beer production"
  )
```
I would defend seasonal naive here, because there is a very strong seasonality in the data, so that seems to be the most likely accurate prediction. (I plotted 4 extra years (16 quarters) to see this even nicer, also I used data after 2000 but checked with starting from earlier and I made the same conclusion)
